issues.legal_issue: A subletting authorized by the contract between the landlord and tenant falls outside the statutory prohibition and does not require validation under the provision governing earlier prohibited sublettings.
material_facts: The respondent conceded that the intermediate subtenant was a lawful subtenant.

The intermediate subtenant’s possession had ended before the relevant amendment took effect, so that subtenancy could not qualify for validation under the provision requiring the subtenant to be in possession at commencement.
The court treated the concession that the intermediate subtenant was lawful as establishing that the original tenant’s contract with the landlord permitted the subletting.
issues.conclusion: The provision validating earlier sublettings applies to sublettings that were not permitted by contract and would otherwise have been prohibited; a contract-authorized subletting falls outside that provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 15(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotels and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, as retrospectively amended, the prohibition on subletting is subject to a contract to the contrary. Section 15(2) is a special provision validating earlier sublettings that would otherwise have been prohibited, subject to its possession conditions; it does not concern sublettings permitted by contract. The possession conditions distinguish those sublettings from contract-authorized ones, which do not require statutory validation.

predicates.rent_control_subletting_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a subletting is prohibited or requires statutory validation under rent-control law.
predicates.subletting_authorized_by_contract: The landlord and tenant had a contract permitting the tenant to sublet the premises.

issues.definition: When a rent-control subletting dispute involves a contract permitting the subletting, the subletting is outside the statutory validation process.

issues.legal_issue: A further subletting by a lawful subtenant may qualify for validation when the subtenant is treated as a tenant for that transaction and the further subtenant meets the applicable possession conditions.
material_facts: The original tenant had sublet part of the premises to an intermediate subtenant, whose status as a lawful subtenant was conceded.
The intermediate subtenant further sublet the premises to the claimant in 1952.
The claimant entered into possession before the 1959 Ordinance and remained in possession when it commenced.
The claimant sought to establish tenancy rights and prevent enforcement against him of a possession decree obtained against the intermediate subtenant.
issues.conclusion: The further subtenancy was deemed valid, and the claimant could rely on it to resist enforcement of the possession decree against him.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15(2) and 5(11)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotels and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, permit the further subtenant to be treated as the subtenant of a tenant for this purpose where the intermediary is a lawful subtenant. The further subtenancy is then within section 15(2) if it was created before the Ordinance and the further subtenant entered into possession before, and remained in possession at, its commencement. Jai Singh Morarji v. M/s Sovani Pvt. Ltd. was distinguishable because the original subtenant there was not in possession at commencement, and the later claimant could not obtain protection through that subtenant. Anand Nivas (P) Ltd. v. Anandji did not defeat the claim because the intermediary was a contractual tenant when making the further subletting; P.D. Aswani v. Kavashah Dinshah Mulla and Waman Shriniwas Kini v. Ratilal Bhagwandas & Co. were inapplicable because they predated the retrospective amendment.

predicates.subtenant_claims_protection_from_possess: A subtenant claims that tenancy protection prevents enforcement against them of a possession decree obtained against an intermediary.
predicates.intermediary_is_lawful_subtenant: The person who made the further subletting was a lawful subtenant of the original tenant.
predicates.further_sublease_created_before_relevant: The further subletting was created before the relevant legal change took effect.
predicates.further_subtenant_entered_before_relevan: The further subtenant entered into possession before the relevant legal change took effect.
predicates.further_subtenant_remained_in_possession: The further subtenant continued in possession when the relevant legal change took effect.

issues.definition: When a subtenant resisting a possession decree derives possession through a lawful subtenant and meets the stated timing and possession conditions, the further subtenancy is treated as valid.
